definition: Demystify means to make something confusing easier to understand.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word demystify. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know demystify should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The coach's playbook sessions demystify the sport for new parents, turning a wall of whistles and hand signals into a game they can follow.
Describing something only tells what it is like; it stops far short of demystifying it, which removes the confusion itself.
Clarify usually tidies one cloudy point; it stops short of demystifying, which dismantles the whole sense that a subject is closed to outsiders.

To explain is the everyday act of laying out how something works, step by step, for anyone who asks. To demystify is more pointed: it strips away the intimidation around a subject that felt closed to outsiders, so ordinary people can finally follow it.

To simplify is to make something less complex — a shorter route, plainer wording — sometimes by leaving true detail out. To demystify is to remove confusion and intimidation while keeping the substance: the subject stays whole, but stops feeling off-limits.

To illuminate a subject is to shed light on it, revealing depth and connections the audience had not seen. To demystify starts from fear rather than darkness: it tears down the sense that a topic belongs only to experts.
to make something feel baffling or magical
to mix something up until it confuses everyone

Reach for demystify when the barrier is intimidation — a subject that feels reserved for experts.
'Explain' covers ordinary telling-how; demystify announces that the mystery itself is being dismantled.

The bicycle co-op's Tuesday clinics exist to demystify repair, and the first tool handed to every newcomer is the one they fear most.
Most arrive convinced that a derailleur is delicate wizardry, adjustable only by professionals in aprons.
So the mechanics begin by taking one apart in front of everyone, naming each piece in plain words, slowly.
The full assembly goes back together, spring by spring, in the newcomers' own hands.
People who walked in afraid to touch a shifter ride home planning their next adjustment.
The machine did not change; the fear did.
